newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Oct vols on U.S. Robotics up.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Oct vols on U.S. Robotics up.

text.p: Investors snapped up calls on U.S. Robotics Corp, driving October volatility higher, as the stock again surged on talk about a faster modem, traders said Thursday.
"October volume is pretty heavy," said Scott Bauer, a market maker on the CBOE. "It's a pretty decent mix" of calls and puts.
He said the pickup in volume drove volatilities in the October series to the 70 to 75 region, from the 60 area where they had been hovering over the last month or so.
"November (volatility) is still trading at 65 to 70, but October's a good five points higher," he said.
By 1130 CDT (1630 GMT), the stock was up 3-1/8 at 69-1/2 on 3.5 million shares. It reached 71-1/8 intraday.
Andrew Schwarz, senior partner at AGS Specialist Partners in New York, said he saw concentrated demand for U.S. Robotics calls.
"The demand is coming from retail customers who are speculating on a higher (stock) price," he said.
On the American Stock Exchange, the October 50 call traded about 1,500 contracts, but it did not trade on the Chicago Board Options Exchange.
The option was up 4-1/8 at 20-1/4 and had open interest of roughly 2,450.
The most active U.S. Robotics option was the October 70 call, which traded a total of 1,740 contracts on the two exchanges.
That option was up 1-3/16 at 3-3/8 on the CBOE and was up 1-3/8 at 3-1/2 on the AMEX. Open interest was nearly 4,400 contracts.
The most active U.S. Robotics put was the October 65, which traded a total of about 660 contracts.
On the CBOE, it lost 7/8 to 2-1/8 and on the AMEX it fell one to two. Open interest was 2,450.
Market talk that U.S. Robotics, which holds a dominant market share in modems, was close to unveiling a faster modem has driven the stock up from below 50 since early September.

On several occasions, the company has declined to comment on whether it is close to shipping a new modem and repeated its stance that the 33.6 kilobit per second modem currently in the market is not the fastest possible.
